<h1 class="hero-name">Noémie Piolat</h1>


I am a doctoral candidate in comparative politics at the [Centre for European Studies and Comparative Politics](https://www.sciencespo.fr/centre-etudes-europeennes/en/) (CEE) at [Sciences Po](https://www.sciencespo.fr/en/), Paris. My research looks at how gender norms and sexist attitudes shape political behaviour in Europe, with a focus on electoral and partisan dynamics and support for the radical right.

My dissertation draws on quantitative and qualitative methods. I use comparative surveys, mainly the European Social Survey, to explore how sexist attitudes relate to political behaviour across European countries, and in particular how the political weight of these attitudes depends on how common they are within an individual’s reference group. In a module designed for ELIPSS, a French probability-based online panel run by the Centre for Socio-Political Data (CDSP) at Sciences Po, I measure individuals’ own gender attitudes together with what they believe is normal in their close networks and in the national population. This allows me to map the gaps between actual and perceived norms in France, and it will inform a planned experiment on how learning where one stands relative to others affects political attitudes and behaviour. Finally, planned focus groups will extend my work on social norms and gender attitudes, to explore how people discuss, justify and qualify their views on gender equality when they express them in front of others.

My research has been published in the Revue française de science politique and the Revue européenne des sciences sociales.

I also teach classes such as Introduction to Political Science, Comparative Politics, and Gender and Political Behaviour as well as graduate courses in quantitative methods.
